question: us-policy-positions:fiscal.balanced-operating-budget
definition: yes = the state constitution or statute requires the operating budget to balance (the governor must submit, the legislature must pass, the signed budget must balance, and/or the state may not carry a deficit into the next year or biennium); no = no such legal requirement.
summarySource: NASBO Budget Processes in the States (2021 edition, Table 9 and notes; the current edition linked from nasbo.org as of 9/28/2026) for the 50 states and D.C.; NASBO Budget Processes in the Territories (2024, Table 5) for Guam, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands; primary constitution and code pages fetched for CA, ID, MN, OH, VA, WA and D.C. No state law change between 2021 and 1/1/2026 that removes a requirement was found.

US-AK.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory). NASBO cites AS 37.07.020(c) (governor) and AS 37.07.014(e)(2) (legislature).

US-AL.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory).

US-AR.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-AZ.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory). Arizona may carry a General Fund deficit; there is no rule to cure it next cycle.

US-CA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional). Since fiscal 2004-05 the legislature may not send, nor the governor sign, a General Fund budget exceeding estimated revenue. The governor-submit, pass and sign requirements are constitutional.

US-CO.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-CT.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory).

US-DC.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional). The Home Rule Act requires the mayor's budget to be prepared so that expenditures do not exceed resources.

US-DE.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-FL.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-GA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional).

US-GU.note: Per NASBO's 2024 territories survey (Table 5), the governor must submit, the legislature must pass and the governor must sign a balanced budget in Guam; Guam has no year-end rule and reports occasional operating deficits.

US-HI.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory). NASBO calls the requirement implied by the constitution and statute; a year may end in deficit if prior balances cover it.

US-IA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-ID.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-IL.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory).

US-IN.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: legislature must pass one (constitutional). This is the weakest form: Indiana may carry annual deficits and relies mainly on the constitutional debt ban.

US-KS.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-KY.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-LA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-MA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-MD.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional). The governor does not sign the budget bill; the enacted budget must be balanced.

US-ME.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory).

US-MI.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-MN.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory). NASBO says the constitutional debt limit implies balance and cites Minn. Stat. 16A.11, subd. 2.

US-MO.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-MS.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-MT.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-NC.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory).

US-ND.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-NE.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory). NASBO marks a constitutional carryover rule but no year-end check; the biennium must balance and a first-year deficit is allowed.

US-NH.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory). The biennium must balance, but it may use prior-biennium fund balances.

US-NJ.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-NM.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-NV.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (statutory).

US-NY.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (statutory); budget signed must be balanced (basis not specified); no deficit carryover at year-end (basis not specified).

US-OH.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory). The constitution caps debt for casual deficits at $750,000 (art. VIII, sec. 1).

US-OK.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-OR.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-PA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory).

US-PR.note: Per NASBO's 2024 territories survey (Table 5), the governor must submit, the legislature must pass and the governor must sign a balanced budget in Puerto Rico; it may not carry a deficit over.

US-RI.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional). The rule is derived from the constitutional cap on borrowing without voter approval; a deficit may be carried into the next year.

US-SC.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory).

US-SD.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-TN.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-TX.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-UT.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional).

US-VA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional). The requirement applies only to budget execution: the governor must keep expenses within revenue over the biennium (Va. Const. art. X, sec. 7).

US-VI.note: Per NASBO's 2024 territories survey (Table 5), the governor must submit, the legislature must pass and the governor must sign a balanced budget in U.S. Virgin Islands; it may not carry a deficit over.

US-VT.note: Vermont is the only state reporting no constitutional or statutory balanced budget requirement, though NASBO notes it has never carried a deficit over in practice.

US-WA.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (statutory); legislature must pass one (statutory). RCW 43.88.055 also requires a four-year balanced budget from the 2013-15 biennium.

US-WI.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional and statutory); legislature must pass one (constitutional and statutory); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional and statutory). The deficit must be corrected in the next fiscal year.

US-WV.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory). NASBO does not mark a governor-submit requirement for West Virginia.

US-WY.note: Per NASBO 2021 Table 9: governor must submit a balanced budget (constitutional); legislature must pass one (constitutional); budget signed must be balanced (constitutional); no deficit carryover at year-end (constitutional and statutory).

unknown.US-AS: American Samoa was not in NASBO's 2024 territories survey, and no fetched primary source confirmed a balanced budget requirement.
unknown.US-MP: The Northern Mariana Islands were not in NASBO's 2024 territories survey; the CNMI Law Revision Commission site loaded but its code text could not be confirmed by direct fetch.
